projects.title: Path Dependence and Divergent Value Formation
Memory Continuity and Persistent Identity in Computational Systems

review.alternative: Inferential error might be entirely path-independent under fully specified theoretical models.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical demonstration of round-tripping path independence under severe model misspecification.

claims.statement: Inferential error under misspecified models is generally path-dependent and decomposes into systematic and non-systematic components.

support.explanation: The source demonstrates that inferential error is path-dependent and decomposes into systematic and path-dependent components.
support.passage: inferential error, of a given belief process vs another (e.g. true probability), is in general not path-independent (not round-tripping despite the given belief process doing so); it decomposes uniquely into twoindependentcompo- nents, one path-independent, systematic and identifiable as a well-known behavioural bias, one path-dependent and not necessarily systematic.

actions.findings: Inferential error under misspecified models is generally path-dependent and decomposes into systematic and non-systematic components. [source-0f17f7655d614a90]
actions.limitations: Empirical validation remains limited to abstract binary inference models and statistical evaluation frameworks.
actions.next_questions: How do specific autobiographical trace structures interact with long-term convergence limits?
actions.reason: Synthesizing retrieved evidence regarding inference constraints and path-dependent preference restriction.
actions.summary: Examining how misspecified models and historical inference constraints restrict the state-space of future preference formation.
actions.title: Path-Dependent Inference and Memory Constraints in Preference Acquisition

proposal.summary: This investigation analyzes how retention and structural inference constrain future preference formation and decision-making heuristics in autonomous systems.
proposal.title: Mechanisms of Memory-Driven Preference Acquisition and State-Space Restriction
